pages.text: The $(item)Ionospheric Processor$() is the heart of a sounding station: a rack of glowing valves that will send pulses straight up through an $(item)Ionosonde Antenna$() and time the echoes off the sky, to tell which bands are open before you call.$(br2)Today it is built and placed, valves aglow; the sky readings are still to come. Until then the teletype's report is your forecast.

pages.title: The ionosonde
pages.text: The $(item)Ionosonde Antenna$() is two blocks tall and goes on coax like a J-pole. It is made for sounding, not talking: on a radio it matches poorly (SWR 3 on VHF, 8 on HF).$(br2)Making a processor takes an amethyst shard among its parts.
